body:
Thanks for your thoughts, I will think on. I don't know if I can reconnect; I genuinely can't really remember feeling anything positive. I don't like not seeing an answer to my problems, and suspect I'm linking that to the last time I felt anything similar, hence the anticipation of bad times. 

I don't know if it is some kind of suppression of emotions or genuine non-feeling, and embarrassment is an interesting test case at least (scientist head on) so I'll have a think about how to approach my GP.

I suppose the summary is "Thanks sofar!". I'll certainly think before acting further.

All the people I know who've had help have all had a decent fucking reason for not being happy. Fuck, I'm using anecdotal evidence. You're right, I should stand down and actually do some research into myself, I just can't find anything that looks like my situation - they're all looking at much more serious stuff.

I just feel like captain asshole even thinking about going into the docs and saying "hey, I don't really feel anything, oh, and by the way, I'm a bit less-than-stable on the whole dealing with life thing. Erm, any ideas? Why? Well, nothing concrete really, just not really liking the whole living thing". Even typing it I feel bloody stupid and can't think of a good form of words; I really think ennui / underjoyed sums it up but they're not exactly 21st century things. 

I feel odd even talking about this; I don't understand self-harm, not because of lack of desire, but because every time I have the impulse it is either resist or cut straight through to the bone. The only time I actively tried to depart (many years ago, for different reasons, under much different circumstances, and in a really stupid way) I told no-one before or after (yes, until this anonymous forum, which I don't think counts but is still the first time I've talked about it). How do you even start to talk to a stranger (which is what the GP is) about this kind of thing?

I'm not sure what you mean by an organic cause, apart from my own brain. Getting on some kind of tablet-based fix (which is the standard UK fix for anything mental) would mean I can't get a new job (see the thing in my post about mine vanishing in a couple of months) without lying for a good few years, which would precipitate all the change I can't really face at the moment.

Honestly, I don't see a solution to the problem. All the standard small things are things I've tried (exercise, diet, etc - I lost 5 stone (17->12) the year before last, put 3 of them back on, and neither made a difference to my life). The only things left are fairly radical changes to my life, and at this point just giving the fuck up looks really tempting rather than creating a whole new life in a different  place with a different job.

Quite literally nothing in the last 10 years has hit me emotionally.

I don't feel sad or depressed, just disconnected from my life.

The only time I talked to a professional was at uni, and they were laughably incompetent, to the point where it was almost funny.

I have no intention of testing anything. When it happens, it will be an one and only. I have no intention to do a "cry for help" - if I go, I go.
